editorial.headline: Adhesive Manufacturing With a Clean Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20291 covers the making of industrial and household glues, and the record leaves it nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20291 is the industrial home for making adhesives and glues. The record defines the activity around production for industrial uses and household tools, with materials that may come from plants, animals, or plastics. Its examples are deliberately broad: starch-based adhesives, bone-derived glues, cellulose esters and ethers, phenol formaldehyde, urea formaldehyde, melamine formaldehyde, and epoxy adhesives. In plain English, this is not retailing glue, applying glue, or using adhesive inside another manufacturing process. It is the manufacture of the adhesive product itself.

That scope matters because the code can be registered across the full scale range in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small domestic producer and a larger industrial adhesive manufacturer are therefore both within the scale map shown here, provided the registered activity remains the making of adhesive or glue as described. The record does not add product thresholds, plant-size rules, technical standards, licensing timelines, tax treatment, or minimum-capital figures, so those should not be inferred from the classification note. The clean reading is narrower and stronger: this code identifies the activity, the examples of adhesive chemistry and origin that fit inside it, and the business scales open to it.

Nationally, the investment signal is straightforward. Nationally, the PMA status remains TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the record treats the activity as open at the national level, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial foreign cap in the slim record, and no special national caveat attached to the 100% figure. The honest sentence is therefore simple: on the national classification and investment fields supplied here, adhesive and glue manufacturing is open to full foreign ownership.

The Bali reading is also clean, and it should not be made more complicated than the record allows. Bali is not marked as blocked for this activity: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium itself is still relevant context because the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. But this activity is not caught by that block in the supplied record. The result is a rare clean alignment: nationally open, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
